clue.text: Have doubts about film with corrosive influence?

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist over glass
rust eats away at iron, a corrosive influence

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious of a film that seems to be a bad influence on its viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be suspicious of something or someone is to lack faith in them.

clue.text: Fish caught in net on lake

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to net a sum is to make it as profit
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A fish is landed in a net on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits inside MAKE to give MACKE, then RE and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The mackerel is a striped sea fish eaten fresh or smoked.

clue.text: Essayist covering president's towering achievement?

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: Sir Richard Steele was an 18th-century essayist who co-founded The Spectator
P is the abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: A writer is reporting on a president's lofty accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside STEELE. The question mark flags the pun: a spire is literally a tall structure built.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire is a tall structure, a feat of building that rises high.

clue.text: Shrill soldiers, jittery? Not good

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers

indicators.note: not good says the letter standing for good is taken away

parts.note: edgy means nervous or jittery

explanation.surface: Nervous soldiers shriek in fear, which isn't helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good, removed from EDGY to leave EDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice is thin and high-pitched, like a reed instrument.

clue.text: Infestation disconcerted an orchestra

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plague of pests upset the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of INFESTATION, put in a new order, make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinfonietta is a small orchestra, or a short symphony for one.

clue.text: Temper? There's a time 23 for it

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Temper? There's a time 23 for it (6)': the stray '23' fits no reading of SEASON as a double definition, so the clue looks misread or cut, and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Temper? There's a time 23 for it

clue.text: Fantastic oil, a Monet, arousing feeling

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marvellous oil painting by Monet stirs the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of OIL, A and MONET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stirs passion or tears in you is moving, full of sentiment.

clue.text: Leading story yielding a surprise

parts.note: a star is the leading performer

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so the story loses a letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A headline news item comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE gives up its A to leave TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to shock or alarm them suddenly.

clue.text: to reveal spice

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'to reveal spice (6)': its opening words are missing, so no wordplay for NUTMEG can be shown, and no source gives the full clue.

clue.text: Tribe with diffident queen, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that what follows is heard, not read

parts.note: diffident is SHY and the queen is ANNE, Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A tribe is joined by a bashful royal consort, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: SHY plus ANNE, said out loud, gives the name of the Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Firm, spicy dish lacking one element

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: lacking means the dish goes without the word for one

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry cooked in a metal bowl
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A company serves a curry that is missing an ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops I from BALTI to leave BALT. A balti is a curry popular in Britain, cooked and served in a wok-like bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 27.

clue.text: Insincere and yet oddly engaging politician

indicators.note: engaging means holding something within, as gears engage
oddly says the three letters of yet come in a strange order

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician seems charming yet hollow at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns YET into ETY, and 'engaging' puts MP inside it. 'oddly' here is an anagram signal, not a pick of odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty words or promises are hollow ones, lacking real feeling.

clue.text: Published note about story behind origin of Bastille as place of imprisonment

indicators.note: about here means going round the outside of another piece

parts.note: a book that is out has been published

indicators.note: behind places the story after the opening letter
origin of points to the first letter of the word Bastille

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
TE is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece tells of a legend about the storming of the Bastille, the famous French prison.
explanation.walkthrough: B plus LIE makes BLIE, which goes inside OUT plus TE. The Bastille in the surface is a fitting distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in its ceiling.

clue.text: Neutral country, say, led by expert queen

indicators.note: led by means coming after, so the first pieces lead

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A neutral nation is headed by a knowledgeable queen, or so it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not an example marker here but the verb STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small neutral nation between two rival powers cushions them from conflict.

clue.text: Part of security system which, if it's free of charge, must be faulty

definitions.text: Part of security system which, if it's free of charge, must be faulty

parts.words: Part of security system which, if it's free of charge, must be faulty
parts.note: a barrier that only works when live with current; if it holds no electrical charge, it is not doing its job

explanation.surface: A security component that is supplied at no cost must surely be defective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free of charge' reads as costing nothing, but here it means carrying no electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire barrier deters intruders by shock, so with no current it fails.

clue.text: Masked hero's friend (grasping most of clue)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Masked hero's friend (grasping most of clue) (4,2,3)': T(HIN)ONTO accounts for THINONTO but nothing gives the final P and there is no definition, so the clue is cut short; no source gives the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Masked hero's friend (grasping most of clue)

clue.text: Newspaper that is filled with day's material

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group
D is the abbreviation for day
IE (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A newspaper carries plenty of the day's news.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside IE to give IDE after ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff cotton fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: Informer, in game with revolutionary dissident, keeping quiet

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: keeping means holding one piece inside another
revolutionary means turned right round, so the dissident word is read backwards

parts.note: a dissident is a rebel
low means quiet, as a low voice

explanation.surface: An informant joins a card game with a rebel who keeps his voice down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns REBEL into LEBER, and 'keeping' holds LOW inside it to make LEBLOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who exposes wrongdoing inside an organisation is an informant of a kind.

clue.text: Argue with wife over right point of view

parts.note: an angle is a viewpoint or slant

explanation.surface: Someone disputes with their spouse about the correct perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places W first in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to dispute noisily or at length.

clue.text: Cold greeting received by comedian on first of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Cold greeting received by comedian on first of (7)': W(C+HI)IT gives WICHIT but 'first of' has no word to pick from and there is no definition, so the clue is cut short; no source gives the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cold greeting received by comedian on first of

clue.text: Main prison reportedly impressive to see

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: the main is the sea, and nick is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: The chief jail is said to be quite a sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA plus NICK, spoken, sounds like the answer. The main is a poetic word for the sea; nick is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes a beautiful view or landscape worth looking at.

clue.text: Member-of herd is after drink around edge of path by a river

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Member-of herd is after drink around edge of path by a river (9)': CHA+R+OLA+IS needs OLA, which 'around edge of path' cannot give (no P in the answer), so the clue looks misread and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Member-of herd is after drink around edge of path by a river

clue.text: Coffee suggested by doctor, then tea

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor recommends coffee, followed by a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is slang for tea in Britain, from the Chinese word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Sailor retaining yen to settle in Maine, perhaps

indicators.note: to settle in means to be placed inside another piece

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: retaining means holding something inside

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A sailor with a longing to settle in New England might do so.
explanation.walkthrough: AB holds Y to make AYB, which goes inside ME. 'yen' looks like longing but is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibly, or perchance, is a way of expressing uncertainty.

clue.text: Deny being some secret agent in retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the letters are read from the end
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A spy who has retired refuses to confirm anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ETAGEN from secrET AGENt, and 'in retirement' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a statement is to contradict or nullify it.

clue.text: Beetle, juddering badly, one parked beside road

indicators.note: juddering means shaking about, so the letters of badly are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen Beetle shaking badly is parked by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juddering' rearranges BADLY into LADYB. The surface pictures the VW car, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladybird is a small, spotted beetle; Americans call it a ladybug.

clue.text: Frightening doctrine largely associated with extreme characters in party

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs or doctrine

indicators.note: extreme characters means the first and last letters of the word party

explanation.surface: A political party's doctrine is chilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts CREED to CREE; the first and last letters of 'party' give PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie and unsettling makes your skin crawl.

clue.text: Purchase volume penned by Confederate hero with passion

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed inside, as by a fence

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
rage is a violent passion

explanation.surface: A book written by a Southern general is full of fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying here but grip or advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means a firm grip or mechanical advantage, as a lever gives.
